findings.problem: G22.117 forks `-b feat/x2 main` while only the session HEAD (feat/s1) tracks .claude/hooks; it pins the HEAD proxy, not the fork start point.
findings.scenario: Reading the start point instead of HEAD turns G22.117 red although that is the intended behaviour.
findings.closure: Closure: lpwttracked commits the kit on main too, or the check reads the fork's start point.

findings.problem: Branch-creation detection misses -B coverage in tests, attached/bundled forms (`-bfeat/x`, `-fb`), the path-only add that creates a branch, and is not tied to the matched call (an unrelated `-b` in a compound command denies a base checkout).
findings.scenario: `git worktree add -bfeat/x .claude/worktrees/x main` on an ignored-.claude project asks instead of denying.
findings.closure: Closure: the detection parses the matched worktree-add call's own args; cases for -B, -bX, -fb, path-only and a compound command.

findings.problem: Ignored-but-tracked .claude/hooks reports a plain ok, hiding a leftover .claude/ ignore line that makes later `git add .claude` skip new kit files.
findings.scenario: install.sh adds a hook; `git add .claude` skips it; worktrees miss it; doctor says ok.
findings.closure: Closure: the doctor reports the rule as advisory when the probe is ignored but the kit is tracked.

findings.problem: The worktree-kit row still says `.claude/` not gitignored and `check-ignore -v`; the code decides with -q plus ls-tree and accepts ignored-but-tracked.
findings.closure: Closure: the row states the -q + ls-tree condition.

findings.problem: WT1/WT2 pin only the check-ignore probe text, not the new ls-tree (tracked kit) condition in tracks/orchestrate/10-worktrees.
findings.scenario: Reverting the ls-tree clause in the prompts stays green.
findings.closure: Closure: a contract needle on the ls-tree condition in each prompt.
